voice: Moving to a new city usually comes down to one question. Where will I actually feel at home? Listings tell you the rent. Commute maps tell you the distance. And if you ask a chatbot, you get the same famous neighbourhoods as everyone else. Transplant tries to answer it with taste.
You start by telling it a few things you love. Here, Khruangbin, Fleabag, natural wine bars and Aesop. Qloo checks each one, so Aesop is the skincare brand, not the storyteller.

Then Qloo maps where people with that same mix of taste live across New York. On its own, that map mostly follows popularity, so Transplant takes popularity out and ranks what's left. For this taste, the answer is Greenpoint.

Each neighbourhood shows the evidence behind it, and which parts of your taste pulled it up. The three picks are in different parts of the city. And if something you love has no signal there, it just says so.
Next come the spots. Places people with your taste go to, numbered on the map. And a first week, built only from places Qloo actually found.
Want somewhere a bit quieter? Just ask. The guide searches Qloo live and shows you every lookup it made. If it can't find anything, it tells you, rather than making something up.
Moving with someone? Blend your tastes. It ranks by whoever fits least well, so neither of you is quietly compromising, and it shows what you both love.

It covers twelve cities, for people relocating and for the teams and agents who help them. Other AI assistants can use it too, through an MCP server. That's Transplant, built on Qloo. You can try it at transplant-taste dot fly dot dev.
